page.layout: One column of Latin verse with headings above each poem (author names with numbers). One marginal note on the left, beside the poem of X. Catchword at the bottom right.

main_text.head: IX. Joannes Curtius Ziegenhainensis.

p.i: FLoribus his redimire caput, pulcerrime Curti, Intactis anui[?], tactis a virgine pulcra, Lectisq; in Charitum pictis & Apollinis hortis, Quam factum bene; namq; dedit tibi Gratia nomen.

main_text.head: X. Nicolaus Lumhardus Berstadiensis.

p.i: LUmharde adesto Laonice: te volo. Tibi hanc corollam Musa nexilem dedit, Carptam è virentis pratuli intonsa coma. QuoFacti è Graeco Poeta. neq; protervum pastor unquam egit pecus, Neq; falcis unquam venit acies improba. Apis una flores veré libat aureos, Puris honestius quos rigat lymphis pudor.

main_text.head: XI. Henricus Crugius Cassellanus.

p.i: URcee, non hedera, mihi non cingende corymbis Thyrsigeri, (Musas sobria vita decet) Urcee, sed lauro Phoebi, castaq; Minervae Condecorande, artis pramia tolle tuae.

main_text.head: XII. Conradus Wrasen Zirembergensis.
main_text.p: WRase[?] praesenti cape letus hora Lauream: pulcro micat haec pyropo, Et levis cespes probat esse numen, Quod regit orbem.
main_text.head: XIII. Georgius Albinus Giessensis.
main_text.p: TV quoq; fer capitis decus hoc, Albine, corollam, Texuit hanc digitis Gratia terna suis. Si quos exercet Musarum cura laborque, Hos manet & merces debita laudis honos.
main_text.head: XIIII. Johannes Mercator Marpurgensis.

p.i: HUc Mercator ades, sequitorq; trahentia fata: Ingenii merces merx erit ista tui.

page.notes: Page number "13" at top left is very faint and uncertain. "anui" in line 2 of IX may be "anni" (printed with a ligature or worn type). "Rase" in XII line 1 is printed with a long s that resembles f; read as Rase. Apollo symbol in IX line 3 is a special glyph, transcribed as Apollinis. Show-through from the reverse page appears in the margins and is omitted.
